findings.claim: The new `dirty: false` requirement makes any commit that changes a suite's case count unable to pass the pre-commit gate — the same deadlock the implementer correctly avoided for `green`, reintroduced for `clean`.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:461-467 — `if said not in [r['wall_s'] for r in rows if r['suite']==suite and r['total']==now and not r.get('dirty', True)]`. `published-band-matches-the-ledger` is tagged ["invariant","fast"], and `.githooks/pre-commit` runs `--suite fast` against the working tree that still holds the UNCOMMITTED new case, so `git_dirty()` (evals/run.py:170-178) is True for every run at the new count. The tree only reaches count N+1 while the case file is uncommitted, so no `dirty: false` row at N+1 can exist before the commit — and the commit is what the check blocks. The committed ledger shows the shape: every row taken while this branch was under edit is `dirty: true`; the two clean rows were only producible because the 133rd/52nd case was already committed at bdd8f41. CLAUDE.md hard rule 2 ("every new failure becomes a case") makes growing a suite the repo's most common operation; it now requires `--no-verify` plus a second republish commit, against hard rules 5 and 7. T-R42's restatement asserts the opposite as settled ("the clean run always precedes the doc edit"), which is false in exactly the case-count-change case.
findings.repro: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED: `_band_wrong({'invariant':(53,p)},{'invariant':53},{'invariant':20.0}, [two dirty 53-case rows])` for p in (13.30, 13.11) -> both return [{'suite':'invariant','published':p,'is_not_a_clean_recorded_run_at':53}] and nothing else; the clean filter is the sole blocker.
findings.acceptance: Adding one adversarial case to `fast`/`invariant` and republishing the band from the run that measured it passes the pre-commit gate in a single commit with no `--no-verify` — e.g. the clean requirement relaxed to "clean, or the only rows at this count are dirty", or the ledger filter accepting the sha the case is being committed at. Watched red/green with a real throwaway case added, run, published, committed. T-R42's "bootstrap worked out" sentence corrected either way.

findings.claim: R1 is not closed: the repair commit itself adds a fourth, unmarked copy of the slack scalar to ADR-019, so the exact defect R1 named still exists — and the code comment asserting otherwise is false as written.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:180 — "when the band is crossed: once per 4.35s, which is a real change in what the tree costs" — added by 4e7120d's §6 rewrite, carrying the scalar without the `one ceiling step (**N.NNs**)` marker. src/browser/eval_adapter.py:373-378 claims "Every restatement of it in either document carries this exact marker and is graded". ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED: `grep -n '4\.35' README.md specs/decisions/ADR-019-*.md` returns three hits — ADR-019:161 (marked), README.md:126 (marked), ADR-019:180 (UNMARKED). The `ponytail:` comment declares this residual hypothetical ("if that ever happens"); it had already happened in the same commit.
findings.repro: rewrite ADR-019:180's 'once per 4.35s' to 'once per 99.99s' -> `_check_published_band_slack()['passed']` True and `_check_published_band()['passed']` True; both gates green with the ADR publishing a 99.99s slack.
findings.acceptance: Either ADR-019:180 uses the graded marker, or the restatement drops the number and refers to the marked sentence; the mutation goes red. A bare-scalar sweep of both documents for the current `_band_step_s()` value would close the class rather than the instance.

findings.claim: The `evals/run.py` dirty-ordering fix — load-bearing for R5's whole clean-band mechanism — changes recorded behaviour with no eval case that could have gone red.
findings.evidence: evals/run.py:261-274 moves `sha, dirty = git_sha(), git_dirty()` above the report write. Swapping the two lines back restores the bug (every `--report` run records `dirty: true` over its own untracked artifact) and nothing goes red: the band check reads the already-committed clean rows, so both suites stay at 1.000. `grep -rln dirty evals/golden evals/adversarial` returns only soak-counts-only-real-completions.json and published-band-matches-the-ledger.json; neither exercises `main()`'s write order. The fix is mentioned only in prose. This is CLAUDE.md hard rule 2's exact target: a real defect fixed without a case.
findings.repro: revert evals/run.py:262 to compute git_sha()/git_dirty() inline at line 274, then run both suites -> both still 1.000
findings.acceptance: An invariant case that drives the history-line writer with a report being written and asserts `dirty` reflects the tree excluding the run's own artifact, watched red against the pre-fix ordering.

findings.claim: The republished `invariant` derivation prints an intermediate on the wrong side of its own rounding rule: a reader applying ADR-013's stated rule to the published `15.0` gets a ceiling of 15, not 20, and `_BAND_DERIVATION` accepts it because it rounds to one decimal.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:97 "The same rule gives 13.08 × 1.15 = 15.0 → **20**" and README.md:146 `| invariant | 52 | 13.08s | 15.0 | **20s** |`. ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED: 13.08 × 1.15 = 15.041999..., which is why `_band_rule(13.08)` is 20; `_band_rule(13.04)` is 15. src/browser/eval_adapter.py:393 checks `round(x*1.15, 1) != product`, so the displayed 15.0 passes. This is the exact mis-derivation ADR-019:102 and T-R39 warn about, reintroduced by the round-2 band source. Round 1's 13.22 -> 15.2 -> 20 did not have this property.
findings.acceptance: The published product shows enough precision to be re-derivable (15.04), in both ADR-019 §3 and README's table, and `_BAND_DERIVATION` asserts `_band_rule(x) == ceiling` rather than only `ceiling == WALL_BUDGET_S[suite]`.
findings.route_note: LOW would normally route to debt. Routed repair because it is a published number that leads a reader to the wrong ceiling, in a document this round is already editing, and the fix is one digit plus one assertion.

findings.claim: The new cited-report size check couples the offline gate to the network-only `live` suite: adding a `live`-tagged case reddens `fast` and `invariant` and can only be cleared by running `live` and committing a fresh live report.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:3157-3161 applies `n != counts[suite]` to every entry of `where_it_stands.reports`, and that dict includes "live": "20260823-000337-live.json", while `counts` is built for (fast, invariant, live, full, all) at :3131. The case is tagged ["fast","invariant"]. Today live count = 9 and the cited report holds 9 results, so it passes; grow `live` to 10 and the offline gate goes red, repairable only by a network run. Before this diff the block stayed green. CLAUDE.md states `live` is not part of the gate, and README:66 documents that the live dependency can be unreachable.
findings.repro: add a `"suites": ["live"]` case file, then run `--suite invariant` -> red on docs-numbers-are-derived with {cites_a_report_of_a_different_tree: ...-live.json, report_cases: 9, suite_now: 10}
findings.acceptance: The size check is applied only to the suites the case is tagged with (or `live` is exempted with the reason stated), so an offline gate never requires a network run to go green — watched red by growing `live` alone.
findings.route_note: LOW would normally route to debt. Routed repair because an offline, $0 gate that can only be cleared by a network run is a gate-integrity problem, and the coupling was introduced by this round's own change.
